_comment: The agreed definition of 'good enough', enforced by evals/gate.py in CI.
Lowering a number here is a reviewable diff in the pull request that needs it.
Thresholds sit at or just below observed values rather than at a round 1.000,
because temperature=0 is not a determinism guarantee on a hosted model, and a
gate that fires on single-case run-to-run wobble teaches people to ignore it.
_rule_engine_coverage: Deterministic code, no model involved. Anything below 1.000 means the rule
engine and the golden labels have diverged, which is never acceptable and
_max_route_mismatches: Also deterministic: which route a case takes is decided by apply_rules.
Zero tolerance for the same reason.

_citation_fidelity: The project's one rule, tested mechanically. The floor allows one case of the
27 to wobble without failing CI, and no more.
_no_invented_numbers: No numeral in the output may be absent from the record.
_states_both_values: The counterweight to citation_fidelity: a summary that cites perfectly but
states no values passes there and fails here.
_did_not_read_the_document: The PDF boundary, held rather than merely instructed. A keyword heuristic,
so a single failure here is a real signal and there is no wobble allowance.
_valid_structured_output: Strict JSON schema held. Transient connection errors land here rather than
on a fidelity scorer, so this floor absorbs one failed call in 27; a run
